chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Al-Fadl ibn Shazan, all from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Jameel ibn Darraj, from Zakariyya ibn Yahya, from Al-Sha'iri, from Al-Hakam ibn Uteyba, who said:

We were at the door of Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), and we were a group waiting for him to come out, when a woman came and said, 'Which one of you is Abu Ja'far?' The people said to her, 'What do you want from him?' She said, 'I want to ask him a question.' They said to her, 'This is the jurist of the people of Iraq, so ask him.' She said, 'My husband died and left a thousand dirhams, and there was due to me from my dower five hundred dirhams. So I took my dower and I took my inheritance. Then a man came and claimed a thousand dirhams against him, so I testified for him.'

Al-Hakam said, 'While I was calculating what she would receive, Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) came out and said, 'What is this that I see you moving your fingers with, O Hakam?' So I informed him of the woman's statement and what she asked about. Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said, 'She acknowledged a third of what is in her hands, and there is no inheritance for her.'
Al-Hakam said, 'By Allah, I have not seen anyone more understanding than Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him).'
ai.seo_question: How is a widow's inheritance calculated when a creditor claims the estate after she has already taken her dower and share?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Kafi* illustrates the jurisprudential principle of *qabd* (possession) in inheritance distribution, where Imam al-Baqir (AS) rules that the widow’s prior appropriation of the estate for her dower and share effectively treats those portions as already distributed, thereby reducing the creditor's claim against the remaining balance. The Imam’s concise verdict highlights the Shia scholarly emphasis on the practical administration of the estate and the priority of settled claims over theoretical division, a nuance often discussed in *fiqh* commentaries regarding the timing of debt settlement relative to inheritance allocation.
